subtitle: Where Scroll and Song Fought Over the Past

panels.shot: split-panel wide, left half a dim Ghazni study, right half a vibrant Rajput court
panels.action: On the left, al-Biruni bends over a manuscript under lamplight; on the right, Chand Bardai stands before armored Rajput nobles, reciting with raised hand; between them, a faint battlefield fades into parchment and verse.

dialogue.text: Between al-Biruni’s quiet ink and Chand Bardai’s thunderous song, India’s wars lived on as a new battlefield: memory itself.

i18n.hi: अल-बिरूनी की खामोश स्याही और चंद बरदाई के गड़गड़ाते गीत के बीच, भारत की जंगें एक नए मैदान में जिंदा रहीं — खुद यादों में।

panels.shot: slow push-in on al-Biruni in three-quarter profile
panels.action: Al-Biruni, dressed in early 11th-century Central Asian robes, sits in a modest Ghazni chamber, reed pen poised over a large open codex, shelves of worn books and astrolabes around him.

dialogue.text: Around 1030 in Ghazni, while Mahmud’s campaigns were still remembered in dust and ash, al-Biruni bent over his Kitab al-Hind, determined to understand the land his patron had so often raided.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1030 में ग़ज़नी में, जब महमूद की लुटी मोहिमें अभी राख और धूल में ज़िंदा थीं, अल-बिरूनी झुककर अपनी किताब अल-हिंद पर लगे, उस देश को समझने पर आमादा जिसे उसका सरपरस्त बार-बार रौंद चुका था।

panels.action: The viewer looks past al-Biruni’s shoulder to pages filled with neat Arabic script and geometric diagrams, a brass armillary sphere and measuring instruments lying beside the codex.

dialogue.text: He wrote not of plunder, but of numbers and stars, of philosophies, rituals and languages, carefully weighing what he heard, warning his readers against exaggeration and careless hearsay.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने लूट नहीं, बल्कि अंकों–सितारों, दर्शन, रीतियों और ज़बानों पर लिखा, सुनी हुई बातों को तौलते हुए, अपने पाठकों को बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर कहने और ऊपरी सुनवाई से सावधान किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of al-Biruni in discussion with an Indian scholar
panels.action: Al-Biruni sits opposite a bearded Indian scholar in simple robes, palm-leaf manuscripts between them, both engaged in earnest conversation in a courtyard lit by late-afternoon light.

dialogue.text: Drawing on Sanskrit texts and debates with Indian scholars, he explained concepts like zero, eclipses and karma, often praising what he found precise, yet noting where accounts conflicted or could not be tested.

i18n.hi: संस्कृत ग्रंथों और भारतीय विद्वानों से बहसों के सहारे, उन्होंने शून्य, ग्रहण और कर्म जैसे विचार समझाए, जहाँ बात नाप-तौल की लगी, वहाँ सराहते हुए, पर साथ ही बता दिया जहाँ बयान टकराते हैं या परखे नहीं जा सकते।

panels.action: Al-Biruni’s face is lit from one side, eyes narrowed in concentration, as if silently testing a claim against his own experience, his pen hovering above the page.

dialogue.text: Al-Biruni stood inside Mahmud’s world, yet his method was his own: to sift, compare and doubt, to separate what he had seen from what others merely asserted.

i18n.hi: अल-बिरूनी महमूद की दुनिया के भीतर खड़े थे, पर उनका तरीका उनका अपना था: छानना, मिलाना, शक करना, जो खुद देखा उसे अलग रखना और जो बस दूसरों ने कहा, उसे अलग।

panels.shot: transition wide shot dissolving from al-Biruni’s codex to a Rajput court
panels.action: The image of al-Biruni’s Arabic manuscript fades into the carved stone pillars of a Rajasthan court centuries later, where Chand Bardai stands before seated Rajput nobles, holding a stringed instrument.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, far to the south and west, another kind of history rose in Rajasthan’s courts, not on paper but in breath and drum: the bardic epics of kings and sieges.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, बहुत दक्षिण-पश्चिम में, राजस्थान की दरबारियों में एक और इतिहास उठा — कागज़ पर नहीं, साँस और ढोल पर: राजाओं और घेराबंदियों के बारों के महाकाव्य।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Chand Bardai performing
panels.action: Chand Bardai, in rich but travel-worn bardic attire, raises his arm dramatically as he recites, Rajput warriors in mail and silk leaning forward, torches flickering against the stone walls.

dialogue.speaker: al-Biruni & Chand Bardai
dialogue.text: “Hear now of Prithviraj, who faced the storm and did not blink!”

i18n.hi: "सुनो अब पृथ्वीराज की गाथा, जो आँधी के आगे खड़े रहे, पलक तक न झपकाई!"

panels.shot: wide interior shot of the court audience
panels.action: Rows of nobles and retainers sit cross-legged, some clasping swords, others lost in the story, a young boy at the back wide-eyed as Chand gestures toward an unseen battlefield.

dialogue.text: Texts like the Prithviraj Raso wove Prithviraj’s battles, captures and escapes into long, ornate verse, binding court, clan and deity into a single tale of loss and defiance.

i18n.hi: पृथ्वीराज रासो जैसे ग्रंथों ने पृथ्वीराज की लड़ाइयाँ, बंदी होना और पलायन को लम्बी, अलंकृत कविता में पिरोया, दरबार, कुल और देवता को एक ही कहानी में बाँध दिया — हार और हुंकार की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chand Bardai pausing mid-verse
panels.action: Chand Bardai pauses, eyes closed for a moment, hand on his chest, as if reaching for an older layer of the song, while younger scribes at the side scratch his words on paper.

dialogue.text: But the Raso as we have it grew over time; later poets added, reworked and expanded, making it a living monument to memory rather than a single eyewitness chronicle.

i18n.hi: पर जो रासो आज हमारे पास है, वह समय के साथ बढ़ा; बाद के कवियों ने जोड़ा, बदला, फैलाया, उसे एक जिंदा स्मारक बना दिया, न कि बस एक आँखोंदेखी डायरी।

panels.shot: split close-up showing al-Biruni’s hand and a scribe’s hand
panels.action: On the left, al-Biruni’s steady hand writes in careful lines; on the right, a Rajasthani scribe’s hand races across paper, adding flourishes as he copies Chand Bardai’s verses.

dialogue.text: One kind of text told readers when it relied on hearsay and where it differed from other reports; the other aimed to move hearts, amplifying speeches and duels that no one had recorded at the time.

i18n.hi: एक किस्म के ग्रंथ ने साफ बताया कहाँ सुनी-सुनाई पर टिके हैं और कहाँ दूसरी खबरों से अलग, दूसरी ने दिल हिलाने का लक्ष्य रखा, उन ख़िताबों और द्वंद्वों को बढ़ा कर कहा जिन्हें उस वक्त किसी ने लिखा ही नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nayachandra Suri at a later court
panels.action: A Jain scholar, Nayachandra Suri, in sober robes, reads from a palm-leaf manuscript of the Hammira Mahakavya to an attentive court, a statue of a later Chauhan ruler behind him.

dialogue.text: By the fourteenth century, works like Nayachandra Suri’s Hammira Mahakavya recalled Chauhan rulers of Ranthambhor, blending record and kavya-poetry to lament defeats and praise steadfastness.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी तक, नयचंद्र सूरी का हम्मीर महाकाव्य जैसे ग्रंथों ने रणथंभौर के चौहानों को याद किया, दस्तावेज़ और काव्य को मिलाकर, हार पर शोक और जज़्बे की दाद दी।

panels.shot: diagrammatic wide shot of a timeline in the background
panels.action: Behind a ghostly al-Biruni and Chand Bardai, a faint timeline stretches, marked with dates and silhouettes: Mahmud’s raids, Prithviraj, later Sultanates, and the periods when the Raso and Hammira Mahakavya were composed.

dialogue.text: Modern historians note the gaps: al-Biruni wrote near his own time, while most bardic versions of Prithviraj and Hammira solidified centuries after the events they describe.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार इन खाली जगहों पर उँगली रखते हैं: अल-बिरूनी अपने ज़माने के क़रीब लिख रहे थे, जबकि पृथ्वीराज और हम्मीर की ज़्यादातर बारावली सदियों बाद जाकर ठोस रूप में आई।

panels.shot: close-up of a modern historian’s hand holding both types of texts
panels.action: An unseen modern scholar’s hands hold a printed Arabic edition of Kitab al-Hind in one palm and a Raso manuscript in the other, a desk cluttered with notes labeled with names like Talbot, Hardy and Thapar.

dialogue.text: Using tools from Cynthia Talbot, Peter Hardy, Romila Thapar and others, they weigh these sources, asking: who wrote this, when, for whom, and with what hope in mind?

i18n.hi: सिंथिया टैल्बॉट, पीटर हार्डी, रोमिला थापर और औरों के औज़ारों से, वे इन स्रोतों को तौलते हैं, पूछते हैं: यह किसने लिखा, कब, किसके लिए, और किस उम्मीद से?

panels.shot: medium shot of al-Biruni and Chand Bardai rendered as translucent figures facing each other
panels.action: Al-Biruni and Chand Bardai appear as semi-transparent figures in a dim archive, scrolls and codices around them, each gesturing toward their preferred tools: an astrolabe and a veena-like instrument.

dialogue.speaker: al-Biruni & Chand Bardai
dialogue.text: “Some truths are counted and tested; others are sung so they are never forgotten.”

i18n.hi: "कुछ सच्चाइयाँ गिनकर, परखकर लिखी जाती हैं; कुछ गाकर, ताकि कभी मिटें नहीं।"

panels.shot: wide shot of a battlefield dissolving into overlapping texts
panels.action: A hazy scene of armored riders and a fort under siege dissolves into layers of text: Arabic prose lines, Nagari script verses, and marginal notes in a modern hand connecting them.

dialogue.text: On the ground, defeats and resistances were brief and brutal; in the centuries after, they were retold, reshaped and sometimes magnified, turning short campaigns into long, shining sagas.

i18n.hi: ज़मीनी लड़ाइयाँ और नुक़सान छोटे पर ख़ूनी थे; पर सदियों बाद उन्हें फिर से सुनाया, गढ़ा और कभी-कभी बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर कहा गया, छोटी मोहिमों को लम्बी, चमकदार दास्तानों में ढाल दिया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a present-day reader in a library
panels.action: A contemporary reader sits in a quiet library corner, surrounded by editions of Kitab al-Hind, Prithviraj Raso, Hammira Mahakavya and modern histories, brows furrowed in thought.

dialogue.text: To honor those who resisted and those who endured, we stand where ink and song meet, testing legend against witness, and letting both tell us how people made sense of loss.

i18n.hi: जिन्होंने टक्कर दी और जिन्होंने सब झेलकर जिया, दोनों का मान रखने को, हम वहीं खड़े हैं जहाँ स्याही और गीत मिलते हैं, दंतकथा को गवाही से टटोलते हुए, और दोनों से पूछते हैं लोग हार को कैसे समझते थे।

panels.shot: closing low-angle shot of shelves filled with Indian historical texts
panels.action: Tall shelves of manuscripts and books rise into shadow, al-Biruni’s codex and a Raso manuscript side by side in the foreground, a shaft of light falling across their worn covers.

dialogue.text: The past does not speak with one voice; it gives us careful observers and passionate poets, and asks us to listen closely enough to know which is which.

i18n.hi: अतीत एक ही ज़बान से नहीं बोलता; वह हमें बारीकी से देखने वाले मज़बूत नज़ीरों और जोश से भरपूर कवियों दोनों को देता है, और कहता है इतना ध्यान से सुनो कि पहचान सको कौन कौन है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Where Scroll and Song Fought Over the Past
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ पांडुलिपि और गीत ने अतीत पर जंग लड़ी
